note: No HSP90 inhibitor reached approval in NSCLC: genotype-defined xenografts predicted EGFR-mutant activity that single-agent ganetespib did not show (4% response, all in ALK-rearranged tumours found afterwards), the docetaxel-combination synergy seen in xenografts failed in the GALAXY-2 phase 3 (OS HR 1.11), and luminespib's ocular toxicity was reproduced in rats only after the clinic had seen it.
label: NSCLC (HSP90 inhibitors)

engagement.model: Genotype-defined NSCLC cell lines and xenografts (H1975 and others)
engagement.note: Ganetespib depleted RTK clients in NSCLC lines; in H1975 xenografts mutant EGFR re-expressed by 72 h after one dose; no patient PD comparison yet.
engagement.short: Client depletion in NSCLC cells and xenografts
engagement.quote: However, after a single dose, reexpression of mutant EGFR occurred by 72 hours, correlating with reversal of antiproliferative and proapoptotic effects.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. No NDA/BLA was ever filed for any member, so whether the model was filed is unknown.
engagement.population: EGFR-mutant (H1975) and other genotype-defined NSCLC lines
engagement.judgement: Opens the track at first publication of an NSCLC-specific model; the ganetespib NSCLC phase 2 (NCT01031225) started in November 2009 on data not then published, and Proia 2012 (epub January 2012) and Graham 2012 (onalespib, epub February 2012) describe sibling NSCLC xenograft work the same year.

engagement.model: Genotype-defined NSCLC cell lines and xenografts (H1975 and others)
engagement.note: Luminespib at its RP2D induced HSP70 in PBMCs and depleted client proteins in tumour biopsies, the readouts the xenografts used; ganetespib raised plasma HSP70 for over a week.
engagement.short: Client depletion and HSP70 induction in patients
engagement.quote: There was evidence of target inhibition in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (HSP70 induction) and tumor (client protein depletion and reduction of metabolic activity by (18)F-FDG PET).
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level. The phase 1 population was mixed advanced solid tumours, not NSCLC. Goldman 2013 (10.1186/1471-2407-13-152) gives the same-drug ganetespib readout, plasma HSP70 elevated for over a week after dosing, which is the downstream tier.
engagement.reason: PD readouts moved in dosed patients
engagement.magnitude_basis: client-protein depletion in tumour biopsies, reported qualitatively
engagement.judgement: Scored same because the model's own readouts (client depletion, HSP70) moved in dosed humans, independent of the later efficacy failure. readout_tier is proximal because tumour client-protein depletion is HSP90's own product; HSP70 induction alone would be downstream. product_in_model is false because the model paper dosed ganetespib and the patient paper dosed luminespib; the pairing is mine (Sessa states the exposure comparison, not the PD one). Healthy-volunteer and mixed phase 1 populations count for engagement under the brief; NCT00526045 has no posted results.

dose.model: Genotype-defined NSCLC cell lines and xenografts (H1975 and others)
dose.note: H1975 xenografts kept ganetespib with a 58-h tumour half-life, supporting weekly dosing, but regression needed consecutive-day dosing; no human exposure comparison yet.
dose.short: Tumour retention set the weekly regimen
dose.quote: In mice bearing NCI-H1975 (EGFR L858R/T790M) xenografts, ganetespib was rapidly eliminated from plasma and normal tissues but was maintained in tumor with t(1/2) 58.3 hours, supporting once-weekly dosing experiments, in which ganetespib produced greater tumor growth inhibition than 17-AAG.
dose.judgement: The model stated two regimen targets: weekly dosing gives growth inhibition only, with client re-expression by 72 h, and consecutive-day dosing gives regression. Every NSCLC trial of the class used weekly (or day 1/15) dosing.

dose.model: Genotype-defined NSCLC cell lines and xenografts (H1975 and others)
dose.note: Luminespib's RP2D exposure matched xenograft-active concentrations and ganetespib reached its MTD regimen, yet single-agent NSCLC response was 4%; the miss is booked under efficacy.
dose.short: Exposure reached; the class still failed
dose.quote: At 70 mg/m(2), the AUY922 concentration achieved was consistent with active concentrations in a range of xenograft models.
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Sessa states the exposure comparison for luminespib; the efficacy failure the status derives from is ganetespib's (Socinski 2013) and later GALAXY-2. Goldman 2013 gives ganetespib MTD 216 mg/m2 weekly and a linear dose-exposure relation but no model comparison.
dose.magnitude_basis: xenograft-active plasma concentration reached at RP2D; no occupancy measure
dose.judgement: Row 'reached, failed, abandoned' of the dose table: exposure reached (stated by Sessa), class failed, no member approved, so dose is contra derived from efficacy and the failure is counted once. A stricter reading scores this as 'target too low': the model said regression needs consecutive-day dosing and patients only ever got weekly or day-1/15 regimens, but no patient-side source states that sustained client suppression was not reached, so I did not. margin_stated is null: Ying 2012 claims no cardiac or liver toxicity at effective doses in mice, but no NOAEL or MTD is public for any member (no NDA).

efficacy.model: Genotype-defined NSCLC cell lines and xenografts (H1975 and others)
efficacy.note: Ganetespib regressed EGFR L858R/T790M xenografts on consecutive-day dosing and ERBB2-driven mouse tumours; the paper named EGFR- and ERBB2-mutant NSCLC as the subsets to treat.
efficacy.short: Xenografts named EGFR-mutant NSCLC as sensitive
efficacy.quote: Ganetespib has greater potency than 17-AAG and potential efficacy against several NSCLC subsets, including those harboring EGFR or ERBB2 mutation.
efficacy.judgement: The track pools the three members' genotype-defined NSCLC cell-line and xenograft work (Shimamura 2012 ganetespib; Graham 2012 onalespib, 10.1111/j.1349-7006.2011.02191.x; Proia 2012 ganetespib plus taxanes, 10.1007/s10637-011-9790-6) as one model system.

efficacy.model: Genotype-defined NSCLC cell lines and xenografts (H1975 and others)
efficacy.note: Ganetespib monotherapy in EGFR-mutant, KRAS-mutant and wild-type cohorts: 16-week PFS 13%, 6% and 20%, 4% response overall, none in the EGFR-mutant cohort the model named.
efficacy.quote: 98 were assigned to cohort A (n = 15), B (n = 17), or C (n = 66), with PFS rates at 16 weeks of 13.3%, 5.9%, and 19.7%, respectively.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level; the protocol's 16-week PFS target is not in the abstract, so the primary-endpoint miss is inferred from the rates and the 4% response. NCT01031225 has no posted results.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: xenograft regressions versus 0 of 15 EGFR-mutant responders

patient_trials.quote: Four patients (4%) achieved partial response (PR); all had disease that harbored anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK) gene rearrangement, retrospectively detected by FISH (n = 1) or PCR-based assays (n = 3), in crizotinib-naïve patients enrolled to cohort C.

efficacy.population: EGFR-mutant, KRAS-mutant and EGFR/KRAS wild-type cohorts
efficacy.judgement: Contra rather than partial-same: the model's stated subset (EGFR-mutant, H1975 regressions) produced no responders and a 13% 16-week PFS, and the only responses were in ALK-rearranged tumours the trial had not selected and the 2012 model had not named. Socinski calls the result activity 'particularly in ALK', hence source_calls_it partial. Later luminespib data on the same kind of model are mixed and do not reverse the track: Felip 2018 (10.1016/j.jtho.2017.11.131) EGFR-mutant stratum ORR 17.1%, Johnson 2015 (10.1200/JCO.2014.59.7328) AUY922 plus erlotinib 16% PR and 'did not meet its primary end point'.

efficacy.model: ALK-driven NSCLC cells and xenografts (ganetespib vs crizotinib)
efficacy.note: Built after ALK-rearranged patients had responded in the phase 2: ganetespib depleted EML4-ALK and beat crizotinib in ALK-driven cells and xenografts, including crizotinib-resistant forms.
efficacy.short: ALK sensitivity modelled after patients responded
efficacy.quote: Importantly, ganetespib overcame multiple forms of crizotinib resistance, including secondary ALK mutations, consistent with activity seen in a patient with crizotinib-resistant NSCLC.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level. The paper itself pairs the model with a patient; the phase 2 ALK responses (Socinski 2013, epub one week later) were presented at ASCO 2011, which I did not verify.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: xenograft survival benefit versus 4 of 8 ALK-rearranged partial responses
efficacy.judgement: Retrodiction (decision 10): the ALK responders were found retrospectively in the ganetespib phase 2 and the ALK model followed, so this is retro, not same, on its own track. No prospective test followed on this track: luminespib's ALK stratum (Felip 2018, ORR 31.8%) was designed in 2010 before this model, and the onalespib plus crizotinib randomised part of NCT01712217 (completed 2017) never posted results or a paper I could find.

efficacy.model: Genotype-defined NSCLC cell lines and xenografts (H1975 and others)
efficacy.note: Docetaxel synergy in H1975 and 5 of 6 NSCLC xenografts went to GALAXY-2: 677 adenocarcinoma patients, OS 10.9 vs 10.5 months, HR 1.11, stopped for futility.
efficacy.short: Phase 3 with docetaxel failed: OS HR 1.11
efficacy.quote: The addition of ganetespib to docetaxel did not result in improved survival for salvage therapy of patients with advanced-stage lung adenocarcinoma.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Year is the registry results posting (2016-07-01), earlier than the 2019 epub.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: xenograft regressions with docetaxel versus OS HR 1.11 (95% CI 0.90-1.37)

patient_trials.quote: The trial was stopped early as a result of futility at a planned interim analysis.

While the study's primary end points were not met, significant prolongation of PFS and OS was observed in patients >6 months from diagnosis of advanced disease, a subgroup chosen as the target population for the phase III study.

The investigator-assessed overall response rate and stable disease rate at 18 weeks were 31.8% and 9.1% in the ALK-rearranged stratum, 17.1% and 8.6% in EGFR-mutant stratum, 9.7% and 22.6% in the EGFR<2 stratum, 0% and 7.1% in KRAS-mutant stratum, and 8.8% and 8.8% in wild-type stratum.
This phase II study of AUY922 and erlotinib did not meet its primary end point.

efficacy.population: Adenocarcinoma, unselected, diagnosed more than 6 months before entry
efficacy.judgement: Same track as the 2013 contra (same xenograft system, now in combination), so strengthens rather than a new status. The model side is Proia 2012 (Synta), which states 'tumor regressions seen with docetaxel' in H1975 xenografts and benefit in 5 of 6 models; GALAXY-1 (Ramalingam 2015) had already missed both co-primary PFS endpoints and the phase 3 population was an exploratory subgroup. The class was abandoned after GALAXY-2 and luminespib supply ended in 2017.

efficacy.model: EGFR exon 20 insertion cell models (Ba/F3 and NSCLC lines)
efficacy.note: Exon 20 insertion mutants depend on HSP90 and luminespib degrades them in cells; a 29-patient phase 2 met its endpoint, 17% response and 38% PR or SD of 3 months or more.
efficacy.short: Exon 20 niche predicted in cells held: endpoint met
efficacy.quote: The results exceeded the pre-determined target rate of effectiveness with 11/29 (38%) patients having a PR or an SD ≥3 months.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Single-arm, 29 patients, endpoint of PR plus SD of 3 months or more against a 20% bar; median PFS 2.9 months; drug supply ended February 2017 and no confirmatory trial followed. The cell paper (Jorge 2018) was published after the trial had enrolled, but the trial was run as its confirmatory test.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: cell apoptosis and client degradation versus ORR 17% and 38% PR or SD of 3 months or more

patient_trials.quote: Among the 29 patients (18 females, median age 60 years) the ORR was 17%, median progression-free survival was 2.9 months (95% CI 1.4-5.6) and median OS (mOS) was 13 months (95% CI 4.9-19.5).

efficacy.judgement: Own track, not a reversal of the failed xenograft panel: a newer, genotype-specific cell model that did better gets its own model_id (brief: 'a newer model that did better is its own track'). model_kind is animal because Jorge 2018 reports cell-line and Ba/F3 models of the same kind as the xenograft panel; no in-vivo arm is stated in the abstract. Scored same because the trial's pre-specified primary endpoint was met, with the weak clinical meaning noted in confidence_note; a stricter reader could hold this at untested on the grounds that the model paper post-dates trial start. Jorge 2018 itself pairs the cells with one responding patient.

efficacy.model: Kras G12D; p53-deficient autochthonous lung adenocarcinoma GEMM (IPI-504 with or without rapamycin, MRI tumour volume)
efficacy.note: Retaspimycin (IPI-504) alone regressed no Kras/p53 lung tumours; only with rapamycin did tumours regress on MRI; no member dosed, no patient comparison yet.
efficacy.short: GEMM: HSP90 inhibitor alone, no regression
efficacy.quote: We show that agents that enhance proteotoxic stress, including the HSP90 inhibitor IPI-504, induce tumor regression in aggressive mouse models, but only when combined with rapamycin.
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text (PMC3233475) read for the lung model: 'none of the single agents investigated in this study exerted a cytotoxic response when administered individually', and Figure 6 shows regression of Kras G12D, p53-deficient NSCLC only with rapamycin plus IPI-504. IPI-504 (retaspimycin) is outside the member list, so product_in_model is false.
efficacy.population: Kras G12D; p53-deficient mouse lung adenocarcinoma
efficacy.judgement: Own track: an autochthonous GEMM whose prediction (KRAS-mutant tumours do not regress on HSP90 inhibition alone) is the opposite of the cell-line and xenograft panel's (Acquaviva 2012: ganetespib 'potently cytotoxic in all' KRAS-mutant lines), so a different system with a different prediction.

efficacy.model: Kras G12D; p53-deficient autochthonous lung adenocarcinoma GEMM (IPI-504 with or without rapamycin, MRI tumour volume)
efficacy.note: Ganetespib monotherapy in the KRAS-mutant cohort: 0 of 17 responses, 16-week PFS 5.9%; the GEMM's no-monotherapy-regression call held; its combination call was never tested.
efficacy.short: KRAS cohort: no responders, as GEMM predicted
efficacy.quote: 98 were assigned to cohort A (n = 15), B (n = 17), or C (n = 66), with PFS rates at 16 weeks of 13.3%, 5.9%, and 19.7%, respectively.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level patient side; my own pairing of an IPI-504 GEMM with a ganetespib cohort. Cohort B is the KRAS-mutant cohort. The GEMM's positive prediction (regression with rapamycin) was never tested with a member drug in NSCLC, so only the monotherapy half is scored. NCT01031225 has no posted results.
efficacy.reason: GEMM predicted no monotherapy effect; none seen
efficacy.magnitude_basis: no single-agent regression on MRI in the GEMM versus 0 of 17 KRAS-mutant partial responses and 5.9% 16-week PFS

patient_trials.quote: Four patients (4%) achieved partial response (PR); all had disease that harbored anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK) gene rearrangement, retrospectively detected by FISH (n = 1) or PCR-based assays (n = 3), in crizotinib-naïve patients enrolled to cohort C.

efficacy.judgement: Same, not neg: neg needs the model's own data for a member drug, and the GEMM was dosed with retaspimycin (sibling, product_in_model false). Not a retrodiction: the GEMM programme was independent of ganetespib's phase 2 (started November 2009) and the paper (September 2011) was not built to reproduce the cohort result; Synta's June 2011 ASCO release predates it but reported the ALK responses, and whether it reported the KRAS cohort I did not verify. Patient-level because the prediction is genotype-specific. Agreement is in direction only and on the negative half of the model's claim; a stricter reader could hold this at untested on the grounds that a no-effect prediction is weakly falsifiable.

safety.model: Mouse xenograft studies with cardiac and liver readouts (ganetespib)
safety.note: Ganetespib's preclinical profile claimed no cardiac or liver toxicity, the geldanamycin liabilities; no patient comparison yet.
safety.short: Mice: no cardiac or liver toxicity claimed
safety.quote: Importantly, ganetespib showed no evidence of cardiac or liver toxicity.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level; epub December 2011, print 2012. No GLP toxicology for any member is public (no NDA).
safety.judgement: The only public animal-safety statement for a member; it is an efficacy paper's claim, not a toxicology package.

safety.model: Mouse xenograft studies with cardiac and liver readouts (ganetespib)
safety.note: Ganetespib's phase 1 DLTs were amylase, diarrhoea and asthenia, with no cardiac or hepatic dose limit; the stated prediction held, but the mice were silent on the GI toxicity that dominated.
safety.short: No cardiac or liver DLT; GI toxicity unpredicted
safety.quote: Dose-limiting toxicities (DLT) observed were: one Grade 3 amylase elevation (150 mg/m(2)), one Grade 3 diarrhea and one Grade 3 and one Grade 4 asthenia (259 mg/m(2)).
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level; mixed solid-tumour phase 1. Socinski 2013 reports one treatment-related cardiac-arrest death among 99 NSCLC patients, and the common AEs (diarrhoea, fatigue, nausea, anorexia) are harms a mouse could have shown but the paper did not report. NCT00687934 not looked up.
safety.magnitude_basis: absence of hepatic or cardiac dose-limiting toxicity
safety.judgement: Scored on the stated prediction (no cardiac or liver toxicity), which held at the MTD; a stricter reading scores the mouse silence on diarrhoea, the class's dose-limiting harm, as contra, and the single treatment-related cardiac arrest in Socinski 2013 as a contradiction of 'no cardiac toxicity'. Kept same at low confidence because one event in 99 patients does not establish a cardiac signal and the model paper was never a toxicology study.

safety.model: Rat retinal damage model (photoreceptor histology, retinal Hsp70, retina/plasma exposure)
safety.note: Built after luminespib's visual disorders and ganetespib's lack of them were known; luminespib and 17-DMAG killed rat photoreceptors and were retained in retina, ganetespib and 17-AAG were not.
safety.short: Rat retina reproduced the ocular-toxicity split
safety.quote: Both 17-DMAG and NVP-AUY922 induced strong yet restricted retinal Hsp70 up-regulation and promoted marked photoreceptor cell death 24h after the final dose.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level; Synta (ganetespib's sponsor) authored the model. In NSCLC, Felip 2018 reports visual disorders in 79.7% of luminespib patients and Johnson 2015 says treatment duration was limited by night blindness; Socinski 2013 lists no visual AE among the common ones.
safety.magnitude_basis: photoreceptor death and retinal retention versus clinical visual-disorder incidence, by drug
safety.population: Patients in HSP90-inhibitor trials with or without visual disorders
safety.judgement: A retrodiction by the paper's own framing ('In human trials certain Hsp90 inhibitors, including 17-DMAG and NVP-AUY922, have caused visual disorders ... others such as 17-AAG and ganetespib have not'), so retro, never same. Whether Novartis's routine animal toxicology flagged retinal toxicity before luminespib's phase 1 is not public (no NDA), so no contra is scored against a toxicology track for the ocular miss; onalespib was not in the rat model and its ocular profile is not scored.

safety.model: Beagle dog repeat-dose retinal toxicity model (ERG, pupillary light reflex, photoreceptor histology; Chugai HSP90 inhibitors CH5164840 and CH5449302)
safety.note: Two structurally distinct oral HSP90 inhibitors gave ERG abnormalities and photoreceptor-layer changes in dogs before other toxicities; sibling drugs, not members.
safety.short: Dogs: ERG and photoreceptor damage on HSP90 inhibitors
safety.quote: CH5164840 induced symptoms that suggest visual disorder, and ophthalmological observation and electroretinography (ERG) revealed loss of pupillary light reflex and abnormal waveforms, respectively.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. The dogs were dosed with Chugai's CH5164840 and CH5449302, HSP90 inhibitors outside the member list, so product_in_model is false; no member was ever in the dog model. The run date of the dog studies is not public; the publication year is the proxy.
safety.judgement: Opens the second ocular track at publication; the same paper states the comparison that the next entry scores.

safety.model: Beagle dog repeat-dose retinal toxicity model (ERG, pupillary light reflex, photoreceptor histology; Chugai HSP90 inhibitors CH5164840 and CH5449302)
safety.note: Published after luminespib's visual disorders were known; the paper reads the dog retinal toxicity as reproducing the clinical visual disorders of the class.
safety.short: Dog retina retrodicted class ocular toxicity
safety.quote: two structurally distinct Hsp90 inhibitors induced a retinal toxicity in dogs after repeated administration, and that visual disorders were also reported in some clinical trials of Hsp90 inhibitors, it would seem highly likely that Hsp90 inhibition induces retinal toxicity.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level. The paper names no member drug: its patient side is 'some clinical trials of Hsp90 inhibitors'. The member-drug patient data are luminespib's: Sessa 2013 phase 1 visual symptoms, Felip 2018 NSCLC visual disorders 79.7%, Johnson 2015 night blindness; ganetespib (Socinski 2013) showed none, a drug-level split the dogs could not address since no member was dosed. NCT00526045 (luminespib phase 1) has no posted results; NCT01124864 results were posted 2016-03-02, after this comparison, so registry_date is null.
safety.reason: Ocular toxicity retrodicted in dogs too
safety.magnitude_basis: ERG abnormality and photoreceptor-layer histology in dogs versus visual-disorder incidence in HSP90-inhibitor trials
safety.population: Patients in HSP90-inhibitor trials with visual disorders; luminespib NSCLC trials carry the member-drug data
safety.judgement: Retrodiction under decision 10: the abstract uses the already-reported clinical visual disorders to interpret the dog finding, so retro, never same. A separate track from the rat model (Zhou 2013): different species, different readouts (ERG, pupillary reflex, clinical signs) and a class-wide prediction rather than the rat's drug-by-drug split. Sibling-drug dosing is allowed by the brief (product_in_model false); the member-drug patient side is luminespib, whose visual disorders in NSCLC (Felip 2018) match, so the harm is scored at class level and not imported. comparison_stated is true because the paper itself puts dogs and clinical trials side by side, at low resolution.
